To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the same protein can have different functions in different cell types and that the same cell type has different sets of proteins and their functions at different stages of development.
the specificity of cell responses is due to the specificity of cell signaling and that the specificity of signaling is due to the unique set of regulatory factors in each cell type.

the same protein is present in many cell types and is regulated by many signal transduction pathways and that each protein has a specific set of regulatory proteins, each with a specific set of modulators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of cell specificity of signal transduction.
the mechanisms of cell specificity and the physiology of signal transduction.
the study of signal transduction networks and the identification of the mechanisms of cell specificity of their action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cell specificity is the rule and not the exception, that it arises at every level of signal transductions, and that it is a fundamental characteristic of living organisms.
cell specificity is the rule, not the exception.
cell specificity is a consequence of cell-specificity in all the levels of regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the specificity of action of a signal in vivo is due to the unique set of signal transduction components in a particular cell type and at a particular developmental stage, to the space and time structure of these proteins, and to the presence of modulating factors.
cell specificity is not an accident of evolution, it is an essential component of the cell physiology.

the complexity of the intracellular world is not a consequence of the complexity of the extracellular world, but is a consequence of the need for the cell to have a complex intracellular world to deal with the complexity of the outside world.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cell specificity of action of signal transduction pathways is the rule rather than the exception.

the cell type specificity of the effects of a given extracellular signal depends on the cell type specificities of the proteins and of their interactions at each level of the signal transduction cascade.
the complexity of cell signaling networks is not a problem but an opportunity to achieve the specificity required to control the diversity of cell functions.
